title: Partial-run replay alignment and delayed trace pairing
description: Handle recordings that start partway through a method by aligning replay time to the corresponding trace offset instead of assuming video time zero equals trace time zero. Also harden recorder shutdown and trace pairing around delayed trace-file creation so manifests can carry enough timing metadata to map video start/stop onto the completed trace reliably.

title: Search replay runs by trace-derived tags such as pillar plate barcodes and run outcomes
description: V1.1 feature: derive searchable replay tags from existing run artifacts without requiring upstream Hamilton method changes. Initial proof of concept should focus on pillar plate barcode extraction from trace files, plus obvious operational tags like aborted runs and error presence. Store tags on runs so users can filter/search replay by tag type and value, including barcode lookup. Scope should cover: (1) define tag schema for visible and internal tags, (2) determine trace parsing patterns/regexes for pillar plate barcode capture, (3) persist tags in local/central replay metadata, and (4) add replay search/filter UI and API support. Design should generalize beyond pillar plates to future method-specific identifiers while keeping the first implementation narrow and fast to ship.

Key decision: central_run_id must be server-issued and path-independent; workstation-local run_id remains a local convenience key only. Central v1 stores binary artifacts on managed disk/share and uses SQL for catalog/workstation/ingest/artifact metadata.

title: Aggregate structured dataset
description: Consolidate JSON summaries from network share into single CSV/SQLite keyed by run_id; include helper metric queries.

title: Polish central replay browse UX for multi-user review

title: Partition local replay runs by machine and surface machine tabs
description: Add explicit machine metadata to workstation camera config and run manifests, store completed local replay artifacts under machine-specific subdirectories, derive final video/manifest names from the matched trace basename plus machine suffix when available, and update the local replay catalog/UI so operators can browse runs by machine without scanning one flat list.

description: Own the central replay server, central catalog/API behavior, LAN browse/admin workflows, and the eventual ingest-service boundary. Focus on server correctness, multi-user robustness, and keeping central replay usable over the network.

description: Reusable CSV/Power BI exports: run volume, median duration, abort %, top errors, sim vs prod mix; document refresh steps.

title: Agent lane: Replay and trace pipeline
description: Own the local replay and trace-alignment core: recorder/run boundaries, manifest contract, trace-derived timing, local replay behavior, and chapter/segment logic. Focus on making one logical run map correctly to video plus Hamilton trace data.

title: Compressed raw trace ingest
description: Ingest full .trc contents into a compact local analytics store with compression so the pipeline can retain raw trace text without keeping large duplicate working copies on the workstation.
notes: Added SQLite ingest batch ledger and per-file ingest event tracking to raw trace store; validated regression and live smoke tests; measured current share at 8.051 GiB raw and estimated full ingested store at ~1.19 GiB.

title: Replace log upload workflow with replay artifact ingestion
design: Replay artifact ingestion now has both sides of the workstation flow. cameras/stage-central-replay.py creates deterministic local staging batches with hashes and run-upload.json payloads. cameras/upload-central-replay.py now ingests pending staged runs into a central filesystem-backed root using cameras/sql/central-replay-schema.sql, assigns server-side central_run_id values, copies artifacts into managed storage/, records ingest_batches/runs/artifacts/ingest_items in the central catalog, and writes run-ack.json acknowledgements back into the local staging ledger. The remaining future work is to swap the filesystem transport for the eventual LAN HTTP service without changing the artifact contract.

title: Harden central replay uploader against stale staging entries
description: The current upload-central-replay path crashes when staged_runs rows reference missing payload_path files, such as deleted or incomplete batch directories. Reproduce the FileNotFoundError on stale run-upload.json entries, then make the uploader tolerate inconsistent local staging state by skipping or marking stale rows instead of aborting the whole upload pass. Include operator guidance for recovering local central_staging state and verify fresh batch-scoped uploads still succeed.

title: Stream local replay videos instead of loading the whole MP4
description: Update cameras/replay-app.py so /api/runs/{run_id}/video serves full-file responses in bounded chunks rather than handle.read(). Keep range support and add coverage for non-range playback/download of large recordings.

title: Unknown pattern monitoring
description: Enhance qc-trace-patterns.ps1 to diff latest run vs qc-unknown-patterns.log and surface newly observed patterns; guidance to whitelist into expected-patterns.json.

title: Prune acknowledged central-staging bundles so workstations do not keep duplicate full-run copies
description: Add a safe post-ack cleanup path for cameras/stage-central-replay.py and cameras/upload-central-replay.py. Once a staged run has a verified central acknowledgement, remove or compact the staged video/trace bundle while retaining only the minimal ledger and ack metadata needed for audit/retry. This should stop staging_root from growing into a second full archive on small workstation disks.

title: Analytics runbook
description: Document pipeline: data sources, scripts, runtimes, add new patterns/metrics, and full refresh procedure.

title: Add replay tag logging across recorder, staging, and replay
description: Add structured logging for replay tag extraction and lookup paths so sim-run validation is debuggable end to end. Cover: recorder manifest/tag derivation inputs, inspect-run-manifests tag summaries, replay catalog refresh persistence, /api/runs search/outcome filters, and central staging payload tag propagation. Logs should make it easy to run a sim method, identify the derived barcode/outcome tags, and confirm which manifest/video was matched during local replay search.

title: Add synthetic end-to-end central replay pipeline test
Evaluate stronger post-run video compression for mostly-static footage
description: Evaluate codecs and post-processing approaches that exploit low inter-frame motion in camera recordings so older replay artifacts compress much more aggressively without destroying operator usefulness.

title: Push HxRun status transitions from Hamilton workstations to the LAN server
description: Future feature after v1: when HxRun changes state on a Hamilton workstation (for example not running -> running, running -> closed), emit a small LAN-visible status event to the central replay/server side so operators can see whether a method session is active without polling the workstation manually. Scope should stay exploratory first: define the event contract, transport, authentication/trust assumptions on the LAN, retry/offline behavior, and whether this should be edge-pushed or server-polled before implementation.

title: Camera replay deployment and retention architecture
notes: Capture the post-prototype camera roadmap: placeholder run selection will be replaced by a real replay catalog, replay artifacts will ultimately upload to a LAN-accessible SQL-backed system, local workstation replay must remain available for low-latency engineering access, and both local and central stores need age-based compression/retention policies.

title: Stream central media responses instead of buffering whole artifacts
description: Update cameras/central-replay-server.py so both full-file and range /media responses copy bytes to the socket in bounded chunks instead of reading the whole artifact into memory. Cover large-MP4 replay/download use and add regression tests for non-range responses.

title: Private GitHub backup
description: Prepare repo for private GitHub: .gitignore, README, Beads; requires maintainer credentials to create remote and push.

title: Tiered replay retention with clip-first hot storage
description: Define and implement age-based replay retention tiers: keep recent full-run MP4s immediately playable, retain error clips and other high-value short segments in hot storage longer, transcode older full-run videos to denser playable archives, and eventually delete or cold-store low-value artifacts after central verification. Cover local and central policy boundaries, catalog state, and operator-visible retention status so replay remains useful while multi-hour runs stop consuming unbounded disk.
notes: Unresolved questions: (1) exact retention ages for hot/warm/cold/expired tiers; (2) what qualifies as an error clip versus other high-value clip classes; (3) whether warm storage stays directly playable MP4 and whether cold storage is true restore-required archive or still a denser playable transcode; (4) which metadata, traces, thumbnails, and clips remain after full-run deletion; (5) how operator overrides, legal/QA holds, and tag-based retention exceptions should work.

title: Offline and Windows 7 camera workstation deployment path
MySQL enrichment pipeline
description: Read-only connector to MySQL (192.168.60.4:3307) and join relevant records into summaries: instrument status, plate IDs, assays; expose in consolidated dataset.

title: MySQL enrichment for summaries
Verify existing central artifacts before reusing them on upload retry
description: Harden cameras/upload-central-replay.py so retry ingest does not trust any pre-existing target file blindly. If a central artifact path already exists, compare size/hash against the staged source before skipping the copy; quarantine or overwrite mismatches only in a way that keeps the catalog bytes and stored bytes consistent; add retry/corruption tests.

title: Camera workstation developer quality-of-life tools
description: Pre-deployment and maintenance utilities for the local camera workstation stack: self-test/preflight, manifest diagnostics and repair, camera probe tooling, and rollout/checklist docs so remote setup and troubleshooting are predictable before central deployment work.

title: Detect consecutive method runs inside one HxRun session without requiring HxRun to close
description: Real-machine validation on C:\QC-main showed that the camera daemon cleanly records a run when HxRun starts and stops, but does not pick up a second method started shortly afterward if HxRun remains open between runs. Current gating is tied to HxRun.exe process lifetime rather than method/run lifecycle inside the same process. Investigate signals from trace activity, HxRun state, or other read-only cues that can distinguish consecutive runs within one open HxRun session, and update the daemon/recorder lifecycle so separate back-to-back runs are captured without requiring the operator to close HxRun between them.

title: Decouple post-run central ingest from the recorder supervisor loop
description: In cameras/camera-daemon.py, auto-upload currently runs stage_runs() and upload_staged_runs() inline after a successful recorder child exit. On slow shares and multi-GB recordings this can block the supervisor long enough to miss the start of the next HxRun session. Move staging/upload onto a background worker or queue so the daemon returns to process watching immediately after recording finishes, while keeping operator-visible status and retry accounting.
notes: Reviewed against commit 139f7eb in C:\QC-deploy. Background ingest queue keeps staging/upload off the supervisor hot path, targeted daemon tests pass, and the commit is acceptable for this task.

title: Single-run replay app with synchronized trace terminal
description: Build a lightweight application that loads a paired run, shows video above a trace terminal, and replays trace lines according to playback time in both directions so seek/rewind reconstitutes the terminal state correctly.

title: Make MySQL enrichment explicitly optional and non-blocking
description: Refactor docs and scripts so the trace analytics pipeline is clearly trace-first, with MySQL treated as best-effort enrichment for optional context and live monitoring.

title: Define HTTP ingest service cutover for central replay
description: Plan and isolate the swap from the current filesystem uploader to a future LAN HTTP ingest service while preserving the staged artifact contract, acknowledgements, central_run_id issuance rules, and central catalog model.

title: Harden central replay API and admin diagnostics
description: Improve the central replay server for real multi-user LAN use: pagination/filtering on catalog endpoints, clearer missing/corrupt artifact handling, better ingest-failure/admin visibility, and stronger status reporting for runs and stored artifacts.

title: Handle recorder rearm exit codes in the camera daemon
description: The merged recorder returns exit code 20 when --enable-midrun-split cuts a speculative segment on trace activity, but cameras/camera-daemon.py still treats any child exit as a completed run and sets run_session_active=True until HxRun.exe exits. That means the daemon never rearms immediately for the next segment, so mid-session splitting is nonfunctional once enabled. Teach the supervisor to recognize the recorder rearm contract, skip post-run ingest for that exit, and relaunch the recorder while the process gate is still active.
notes: Current deployment/runtime branch already handles recorder rearm exit codes and immediate relaunch behavior in cameras/camera-daemon.py. Targeted daemon tests covering exit code 20 passed during review.

title: Split long-lived HxRun sessions into distinct runs
description: Detect and split cases where HxRun.exe stays open across multiple assay runs so the workstation recorder emits one replay artifact per actual run instead of one long combined capture.

title: Detect post-run idle boundaries without truncating trace-finalization capture
description: Handle cases where HxRun.exe stays open after a method appears to end by detecting likely end-of-run or idle boundaries without stopping recording so early that trace pairing breaks. Persist the inferred logical run-end timestamp and reason, continue capture until trace finalization is safe, and emit enough timing metadata for later trimming/alignment rather than assuming recorder stop equals method end.
design: Important recorder cases to support: (1) the trace file may not be finalized until HxRun.exe closes or another run starts; (2) when HxRun.exe stays open for multiple runs, the previous run's trace may appear or finish writing while HxRun is still open; (3) a new-method trigger should cut/finalize the current recording, run normal pairing/manifest processing for the completed run, and start a new capture for the new run; (4) if that trigger was a false positive and no corresponding log file materializes, the speculative recording segment should be discarded rather than kept as a bogus run. This task owns boundary detection and safe finalization timing, not final replay offset math.
notes: Need validation on exact Hamilton behavior: whether the prior trace file is first created at next-run start and only completed later, or fully written immediately at next-run start. User may confirm after observing a live workstation. Implementation should therefore tolerate both 'trace appears mid-session' and 'trace mtime advances until next transition' behaviors.

title: Hybrid replay source mode for target vs central media
description: Support runs that first appear in the LAN replay UI backed by media on the target workstation, then switch to central-hosted playback after archival upload completes. Define source-state fields, online/offline target handling, access/control assumptions, and replay fallback rules so immediate visibility does not require copying every artifact first.

title: Avoid re-hashing the full replay archive on every auto-upload pass
description: The current staging path walks every ready manifest and recomputes SHA-256 for each manifest/video/trace before it can decide whether the run was already staged. On consumer workstations this turns each post-run auto-upload cycle into repeated full-disk reads of historical MP4s. Add a cheaper duplicate check keyed by persisted file metadata or manifest state so only new or changed runs are hashed/copied.

title: Persistent machine validation log for camera v1
Stabilize Beads auto-flush and concurrent CRUD on Windows
description: While creating camera scalability issues on 2026-04-21, Beads intermittently failed with 'failed to open database: sqlite3: unable to open database file' during concurrent creates and also logged auto-flush rename failures: '.beads\\beads.base.jsonl.tmp... -> .beads\\beads.base.jsonl: Access is denied'. Investigate Windows file-locking/daemon/export-hash interactions so issue creation and JSONL sync remain reliable.

title: Explore whether active HxRun method names can be surfaced to the LAN server
description: Future exploratory feature after v1: investigate whether the workstation can reliably determine the currently running Hamilton method name while HxRun is active and expose it to the LAN status surface. Confirm what signal is available (process metadata, window title, trace/log side channel, or other safe read-only source), how accurate/timely it is, and whether privacy/operator confusion risks make it unsuitable. Do not assume this is feasible until the exploration is complete.

title: Replace placeholder run picker with ingest-backed replay catalog
description: Replace the current manifest directory placeholder list with a real run catalog sourced from ingested replay artifacts so operators browse durable runs instead of filesystem stubs.

title: Agent lane: Deployment and workstation runtime
description: Own the workstation-side operational surface for the camera stack: rollout/update flow, daemon runtime behavior, version/status visibility, OS compatibility, and local tooling needed to keep capture machines reliably running the intended code.

Stamp machine alias during workstation camera bootstrap
Workstation recorder daemon and auto-start
description: Package the recorder as an always-on workstation-local background process or service that waits for HxRun.exe, records each run automatically, writes paired run artifacts, and restarts cleanly after reboot so the local replay flow works without operators launching scripts by hand.

title: Derive replay run IDs from stable metadata instead of absolute paths
description: Change cameras/inspect-run-manifests.py and any mirrored replay-id derivation so local_run_id stays stable when the repo path, install root, or runs_root moves. Base identity on stable run metadata and machine-scoped filenames/timestamps rather than manifest/video/trace absolute paths, then verify stage-central-replay dedupe continues to work across workstation cutovers.

title: Handle duplicate-manifest replay catalog refresh after stable run IDs
description: After path-stable replay run IDs landed, cameras/replay-app.py refresh_catalog() still inserts with ON CONFLICT(manifest_path) while runs.run_id remains the primary key. If the same logical run exists twice under one runs_root, refresh_catalog() raises UNIQUE constraint failed: runs.run_id instead of tolerating duplicate manifests during cutover/backfill scenarios. Fix the local replay catalog so duplicate manifests for one logical run do not crash refresh, and add regression coverage.

title: Single-camera log/video sync verification
notes: Harden clip/log association so it matches clip intervals to trace windows instead of nearest-line only. Add a repeatable regression test around the example Hamilton trace and document the real-camera sync verification path before multi-camera work.

title: Retention gate after verified ingest
description: Define and automate the conditions under which raw network trace files can be deleted or archived after successful ingest, validation, and compact local persistence.

title: Package central replay server for host deployment
description: Turn the current browse server into a deployable central-host service: stable config path, startup wrapper, host-local logs, fixed upload-root/catalog conventions, and a basic health-check path so one machine can reliably host the LAN replay site.

title: Build packaged legacy camera runtime path
notes: Reviewed in C:\QC-deploy on branch codex/deploy at commit 9ea60d6 and re-verified on 2026-05-07. Packaged legacy runtime builder and wrapper resolution are implemented in this branch and documented in C:\QC-deploy\tmp\agent-handoffs\deployment-agent-20260423.md. Fresh verification covered daemon tests, bootstrap tests, and config inspection. Remaining risk is end-to-end validation on a real Windows 7 host, not missing repo implementation.

title: Implement v1 QC ticket intake schema storage and submit/list flows
Auto-register completed runs with central replay
description: When the workstation recorder daemon finishes a run and trace pairing succeeds, publish the run into the central replay catalog immediately without waiting for a manual batch command. Capture enough metadata for the LAN UI to show the run as soon as it closes, mark its archival state, and leave room for background upload/retry behavior afterward.
notes: Implementation direction: have the workstation camera daemon push explicit LAN status updates to the central replay server instead of trying to infer pending work from SMB traffic. Add lightweight heartbeat plus event-driven updates so the server can track workstation identity, current state, local IP, current run id, profile, timestamps, and last error before full media upload completes. Proposed states: idle, recording, pending_upload, uploading, available, failed. This should become the main path for immediate central registration/status while QC-xkj remains the media archival/upload path.

title: Implement local-first replay app for Hamilton workstations
description: Keep a local replay application installable on each Hamilton workstation so engineers can inspect fresh runs immediately without waiting for central ingestion lag.

title: Define retention and compression policy for central replay archive
description: Define central replay archive retention and the cutoff when older video/trace artifacts are recompressed for denser storage while preserving replayability from the LAN catalog.

title: Standardize workstation update and cutover flow
description: Define and implement a repeatable way to deploy and restart workstation camera code without ambiguity about which branch/commit is live. Cover install/update commands, daemon restart behavior, post-update verification, and how to avoid 'repo merged but workstation still on old branch' drift during beta rollout.

title: Visualize Codex worktrees and agent positions on git graph
On-demand restore flow for archived full-run replay
description: Support replay runs whose full-length video has been moved to cold or tightly compressed storage. Keep short error clips immediately playable in the UI, expose that the full run requires restore/preparation, and add the server/workstation flow to materialize a playable MP4 on demand with visible status and auditability.
notes: Unresolved questions: (1) UI states for hot/warm/cold/restoring/error; (2) who is allowed to request restore and whether restore should be automatic on play click or explicit; (3) expected restore-time targets for local versus LAN-hosted runs; (4) where restored playable MP4s live, how long they persist, and how cache eviction works; (5) whether restored full runs should rehydrate from true cold archive or from a denser warm playable transcode when available.

title: Workstation rollout checklist and rollback docs
description: Document remote installation, validation, common failure modes, and rollback/uninstall steps for the local Hamilton camera stack.

title: Camera source abstraction and workstation config
description: Move camera and Hamilton log source details into config so the recorder and replay flow tolerate different log paths today and future camera hardware swaps with minimal code changes.

title: Replay run picker and camera view modes
description: Add a run selection UI plus camera display tabs that let operators switch between individual cameras or an all-cameras view while keeping the synchronized trace terminal below the video region.

title: Network deployability and multi-user access
description: Package the analytics system so other users on the network can run it from their own machines with minimal setup: shared/raw-store access, local or shared config, dependency/bootstrap path, and documented multi-user deployment/upgrade flow.

title: Prevent one HxRun session from fragmenting into multiple top-level runs during trace-driven rearm
description: Real-machine validation on qc-storage showed one simulated HxRun session producing five separate .mp4/.run.json pairs under cameras/video_clips. The daemon stayed healthy, but camera-recorder repeatedly returned RECORDER_REARM_EXIT_CODE=20 due to 'Mid-session trace activity detected; signaling daemon to rearm recorder.' The result is multiple top-level runs for one operator session instead of one logical run with internal segmentation. Investigate whether --enable-midrun-split should be disabled for v1, gated more narrowly, or represented as segments inside a single manifest rather than separate runs.

title: Agent lane: Storage and retention
description: Own storage pressure, artifact integrity, deduplication, retention, and bounded local/central disk usage for the camera replay stack. Focus on consumer-workstation disks, safe cleanup, and keeping catalog metadata consistent with stored bytes.

title: Camera workstation preflight and self-test
description: Add one command that validates effective camera config, repo-local storage paths, ffmpeg availability, runs-root writability, daemon/replay startup, and manifest health so a workstation can be checked before or after rollout.

title: Manifest diagnostics and stale-run cleanup
description: Add utilities that enumerate replay manifests with missing videos or traces, explain why a run is unhealthy, and optionally prune or quarantine stale manifests safely.

title: Scalability issues
description: Track replay-stack correctness and storage scalability work needed before wider beta use. Scope includes streaming large media instead of buffering full files, stable run identity across workstation path changes, duplicate-safe and artifact-verified central ingest retries, bounded local staging storage, and avoiding repeated full-archive hashing/copying on consumer disks.

title: Hybrid replay chapters and idle compaction
description: Deliver the next replay/storage slice for Hamilton camera runs: keep one logical run per HxRun session, derive trace-based chapters plus active/idle windows, compact long idle windows aggressively for storage, preserve short-term full-detail retention, and expose the result as one logical replay timeline locally and centrally.
design: This epic is intentionally narrower than the broader replay rewrite and retention architecture work already in Beads. It should reuse continuous per-run capture, post-run trace pairing, and existing retention architecture tickets rather than duplicating them. The missing implementation surface is chapter/segment metadata, post-run idle compaction artifacts, and replay/catalog support for those derived artifacts.

title: Trace-derived chapter and active/idle window extraction
description: Parse completed Hamilton traces into deterministic replay chapters and classify windows as active or idle so long incubations/waits can be handled differently from operator-action phases.
acceptance_criteria: Given representative .trc fixtures, the extractor emits ordered windows with start/stop offsets, phase labels, and active-vs-idle classification; runs without recognized idle phases degrade cleanly to one active window; tests lock the behavior.
notes: First pass landed in C:/QC-Boundary-Detection: added trace-derived chapters/active-idle segments in cameras/trace_replay.py, recorder manifest fields, replay API/catalog backfill, and targeted tests. No compaction artifacts or central ingest changes yet.

title: Manifest and local catalog schema for chaptered replay artifacts
description: Extend the local run manifest and replay catalog so one logical run can advertise chapters, segment windows, storage tier metadata, and retention state without changing run identity.
acceptance_criteria: One completed run can persist normalized chapter/segment metadata in the manifest; the local catalog indexes the new fields without breaking existing runs; legacy manifests remain readable; tests cover both upgraded and legacy cases.
notes: Added a shared hybrid replay manifest contract (hybrid-replay.v1) with replay_capabilities, normalized old manifests in recorder/replay/inspect paths, staged normalized manifests for central ingest, persisted manifest version/capabilities plus segment counts in the central catalog, and added compatibility/round-trip regression coverage.

title: Segment-aware local replay timeline and idle-span UX
description: Update the local replay app to present one logical run timeline with chapter markers, collapsed idle spans, and explicit drill-in to compacted or full-detail windows when available.
acceptance_criteria: The local replay UI can render chapter markers and idle spans from manifest/catalog metadata; default playback skips or collapses idle spans without losing the logical timeline; operators can explicitly open an idle window; tests cover run detail API changes and UI-facing payload shape.
notes: Backward-compatibility checks re-run and passing. Next slice is the first user-visible hybrid replay behavior: segment-aware timeline presentation and idle-span UX on top of the versioned manifest contract.

title: Central replay artifact model for derived compacted segments
description: Extend staging, upload, and central replay catalog behavior so one logical run can carry derived compacted replay artifacts, retention-state metadata, and source-vs-derived playback choices without guessing from filenames.
acceptance_criteria: Staging/upload can carry compacted replay derivatives alongside the canonical run manifest; the central catalog records enough metadata to distinguish source artifacts from derived replay artifacts; central replay APIs remain backward compatible for runs that only have the original artifact set.

title: Central replay catalog schema and ingest contract
description: Define the SQL tables, identifiers, artifact layout, and workstation upload contract for the LAN replay server so local run manifests can ingest cleanly into a shared catalog.

title: Local live camera view during or outside runs
description: After the local replay v1 path is stable, add a live local camera viewing mode on each Hamilton workstation so engineers can watch the camera feed either alongside active runs or by itself without waiting for replay artifacts.

title: Central replay server API and operator workflows
description: Define the operator-facing LAN replay API, browse flows, and workstation-to-server operational model for browsing, refreshing, and troubleshooting replay artifacts over the network.
design: Initial operator/API contract captured in cameras/CENTRAL-REPLAY-API.md. V1 split: ingest API for workstation uploads, catalog/replay API for LAN browse, admin API for quarantine/archive/ingest troubleshooting. Media endpoints must support byte ranges and trace events should be served separately from raw trace files.

title: Low-disk emergency cleanup path for recorder workstations
description: Add a workstation-side low-disk emergency retention path so camera machines do not stop recording when normal age-based cleanup cannot keep up. Define free-space thresholds, cleanup order, invariants for what must never be deleted without central acknowledgment, operator-visible status/logging, and the final fail-safe behavior if disk pressure remains critical after emergency cleanup.

title: Automate post-run central replay upload
description: Trigger central replay archival upload automatically after the workstation daemon closes and pairs a run, either inline from the daemon or via a scheduled/background task. Cover queueing, retry behavior, duplicate-safe staging/upload, operator-visible status, and the boundary between immediate central registration and eventual media archival so manual batch commands are no longer required for normal operation.
notes: Implemented initial inline daemon automation path. After a successful recorder child exit, camera-daemon can now auto-stage completed runs and auto-upload pending staged runs when central_ingest.auto_upload_on_run_complete is enabled. The staging ledger still handles duplicate-safe signatures and pending-run retries, and daemon status now records the last stage/upload batch summary for operator diagnostics.

title: Harden workstation camera installation path
description: Use the real remote-workstation rollout findings to make camera deployment reliable and close to one-click. Capture and fix the gaps we hit in practice: ffmpeg/runtime dependency bootstrap instead of assuming bundled dist artifacts; repo-root-relative defaults instead of inherited C:\\QC paths; daemon/task install behavior that clears stale stop files and stops stale processes before restart; safer local override generation and normalization so camera source/label values are not mangled by shell quoting; better validation commands that test raw ffmpeg capture, one-frame probe, recorder, and daemon layer by layer; clearer handling when a foreground recorder is stopped before manifest creation; and operator-facing diagnostics that make it obvious which layer failed. Document the differences between original assumptions and what the real installation actually required on the target machine.

title: Controlled engineering beta hardening
description: Track the short list of non-UI gates for opening the Hamilton camera system to a small internal engineering beta: local storage pressure, workstation version/status visibility, deployment/update discipline, and rollout verification. Reuse existing storage and replay issues where possible rather than duplicating them.

title: Expose deployed workstation version and recorder contract status
description: Make it obvious which code/config a camera workstation is actually running. Extend status/preflight tooling so operators can see the deployed git commit or build stamp, effective config roots, manifest contract version support, and whether the daemon/child recorder have picked up the latest rollout.
